text.title: documentation Core Rules
text.summary: Eight rules for the Faion CLAUDE.md + AGENTS.md documentation convention.

rule.statement: `CLAUDE.md` in every directory contains exactly one line: `@AGENTS.md`. No other content.
rule.rationale: Convention forks confuse Claude Code's auto-loader. One canonical entrypoint pattern keeps the agent's mental model stable.

rule.statement: `AGENTS.md` is 20-80 lines (hard cap: 120). It covers: purpose, file table, key types, commands, gotchas. Longer content goes under `.agents/` referenced by `.agents/INDEX.md`.
rule.rationale: Agents auto-load AGENTS.md at every session start. Above ~80 lines, the context cost compounds across sessions; below 20, it's not useful routing.

rule.statement: AGENTS.md MUST include a `## Files` table with one row per significant source file: path, purpose. Generated / vendored dirs are listed with their generator.
rule.rationale: The file table is the single most useful section for agents. Without it, the agent grep-walks the dir; with it, it grep-targets.

rule.statement: Every directory containing source code has CLAUDE.md + AGENTS.md — not just repo roots, but subpackages, module folders, test dirs. Skip only empty `__init__.py`-only dirs with no logic.
rule.rationale: Partial coverage produces inconsistent agent behaviour. The pair is cheap (under 80 lines); the cost is paid once per dir.

rule.statement: Deep architecture / API references / decision records live under `.agents/` with `.agents/INDEX.md` as the catalogue. AGENTS.md mentions the INDEX path.
rule.rationale: Keeps AGENTS.md short while making heavy reference material discoverable on demand.

rule.statement: When the project has source-bearing directories lacking the pair, the team has agreed `CLAUDE.md = @AGENTS.md`, and AI agents read these files in sessions, the documentation pass MUST run on a named trigger - a new source-bearing directory created, or a file named in any `## Files` table renamed or deleted - and MUST produce the 02-output-contract record computed from the tree, not estimated: `claude_md_aliases` true only if every `CLAUDE.md` is exactly `@AGENTS.md`, `agents_md_lines` from a line count of each `AGENTS.md` (20-80, hard cap 120), `file_table_present` from a `## Files` heading with one row per significant file, `per_module_coverage_pct` as directories holding both files over all source-bearing directories (empty `__init__.py`-only dirs excluded) and at least 90, and `agents_folder_indexed` whenever `.agents/` exists.

rationale.source: Claude Code docs - CLAUDE.md memory; Faion documentation convention

rule.rationale: The pair is loaded at every session start, so an `AGENTS.md` that drifted past 120 lines or a file table naming deleted files (fm-02, fm-05) taxes every session until someone notices. Tying the pass to the rename and new-directory events, and computing the fields from the tree, catches the drift on the commit that caused it.

rule.statement: When the preconditions hold but a required field cannot be computed - no output target path names which directories are in scope, no owner is named to maintain the pair, or the source-bearing / generated boundary is undefined because vendored and generated directories are not listed with their generator so the `per_module_coverage_pct` denominator is unknown - the pass MUST block naming the missing Prerequisites row, and MUST NOT emit a record with `per_module_coverage_pct` computed over the repo root alone or `agents_md_lines` measured on the root `AGENTS.md` only.
rule.rationale: Coverage measured over the root directory is 100% with one file and reproduces fm-04 (only the repo root covered) as a passing record. An undefined generated-code boundary lets a vendored tree count as uncovered source or covered documentation depending on who runs the pass, so the number is not comparable between runs.

rule.statement: When any Applies-If fails or any Skip-If holds - a single-file script with no surrounding directory, a vendored or generated directory whose edits would be overwritten, or an empty `__init__.py`-only directory with no logic - the methodology MUST NOT be applied to that directory; the skip MUST be recorded against the evidence anchor (commit or ticket) naming the failed precondition, the directory MUST be excluded from the `per_module_coverage_pct` denominator and, for vendored or generated code, listed with its generator in the parent `## Files` table rather than given its own pair, routing repo-wide convention questions to `best-practices-2026`.

rationale.source: Faion documentation convention; Claude Code docs - CLAUDE.md memory

rule.rationale: A pair written into a generated directory is deleted on the next build and shows up as fm-05 (stale references) in the parent; an unrecorded skip shows up as a coverage drop nobody can explain. Listing the generator in the parent table is what lets an agent know not to edit there.
